core_obligations: Fix a nonzero element x of the domain R and note that x : R to R is injective (proof line 4919).
Use flatness of M over R to conclude that x : M to M is injective as well (proof lines 4919-4921).
Read off the statement: no nonzero element of M is killed by a nonzero element of R, hence M is torsion free (proof lines 4920-4921).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the 57 public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers 4913-4922. The nearest records are 336 (4721-4764, tag 0H7R, descent of projectivity) and 362 (4294-4367, tag 05LT, finite-stage descent of flatness along a filtered colimit); neither proves the flat-implies-torsion-free implication over a domain.
difficulty_reason: The statement is a one-line implication, flat implies torsion free over a domain, and the proof is a short but genuinely two-step argument (statement lines 4913-4915, proof lines 4918-4922). The decisive move is to test flatness on the principal multiplication maps x : R to R, which are injective because R is a domain with x nonzero; flatness transports that injectivity to x : M to M, and that is exactly what forbids a nonzero element of M from being killed by a nonzero ring element (proof lines 4919-4921). It is not a formal consequence of the definition of flatness alone: the domain hypothesis is what makes multiplication by x injective on the ring, and it is used at that single point. The proof reaches the conclusion directly, with no remaining verification.
